newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suspected Algerian Moslem radicals in French court.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Algerian Moslem radicals in French court.

text.p: Seven Algerians accused of trafficking in false identity papers and weapons for Algeria's banned Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) went on trial in Paris on Thursday.
The defendants face charges of conspiring in terrorist activities.
Some of them are accused of being linked to a wave of bombings blamed on Algerian Moslem fundamentalists in 1995 in France, and face sentences of up to 10 years in jail.
The alleged network, based in the northern Lille region, was dismantled between March 1994 and last February following an investigation into drugs trafficking.
Prosecutors say most of the defendents are members or supporters of the FIS and of the Algerian Fraternity in France, a group believed close to the FIS.

The 1995 bomb attacks which killed eight people in France have been blamed on the Armed Islamic Group (GIA), the most ruthless of Algerian rebel organisations. The GIA recently threatened more attacks, following a bomb explosion on a Paris commuter train which killed four people.
